title: Liouville-Jacobi determinant of a propagator as exponential of integrated trace; CNF instantaneous change of variables
expression_sketch:
Linear system Phi'(t) = A(t)*Phi(t) on a real interval, A continuous n x n. Liouville / Abel-Jacobi-Liouville:
  det(Phi(t)) = det(Phi(t0)) * exp( Integral(tr(A(s)), (s, t0, t)) ).
Jacobi formula (any C^1 invertible Y(t)):
  d/dt det(Y) = det(Y) * tr(Y**(-1) * Y').
Constant-A / matrix-exponential member:
  det(exp(A)) = exp(tr(A)),
  det(exp(t*A)) = exp(t*tr(A)).
Continuous normalizing flow / instantaneous change of variables (Chen et al. Neural ODE 2018; Grathwohl et al. FFJORD):
  d/dt log p(x(t)) = - tr(Df(x(t), t)),
which for linear f(x)=A x is -tr(A) and integrates to the Liouville factor. Scalar 2x2 probe:
  A = diag(alpha, beta), Phi(t)=diag(exp(alpha*t), exp(beta*t)),
  det(Phi(t)) - exp((alpha+beta)*t) == 0.
Rotation probe: A = [[0,-1],[1,0]], tr(A)=0, det(exp(t*A))=1.
latent_structure: Master object: the scalar function t |-> det(Phi(t)) of a fundamental matrix, reconstructed from the trace of the generator by one exponential. Jacobi supplies the infinitesimal form (derivative of det via trace of the logarithmic derivative). The CNF log-density ODE is the same identity on the Jacobian of a flow. Multiple members: Wronskian/det, exp o tr, instantaneous log-density.

function_domains.exp: entire; applied here to the scalar tr(A) and to matrices
function_domains.p: positive C^1 density along the flow (CNF member)

nonzero_conditions.statement: Jacobi form with Y**(-1) requires det(Y(t)) != 0; for a fundamental matrix this is equivalent to det(Phi(t0)) != 0, which is preserved by Liouville
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Hartman, Ordinary Differential Equations, Sec. IV.1 (Liouville); Wikipedia Liouville's formula; Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 1.13(c) / standard det(exp(A))=exp(tr(A))

nonzero_conditions.statement: CNF log p requires p > 0 along the trajectory
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Chen, Rubanova, Bettencourt, Duvenaud, NeurIPS 2018, arXiv:1806.07366, instantaneous change of variables; Grathwohl, Chen, Bettencourt, Duvenaud, ICLR 2019, arXiv:1810.01367, eq. (2)

positivity_conditions.statement: CNF density p is positive so that log p is defined on the real line
positivity_conditions.label: DECLARED
positivity_conditions.source: Grathwohl et al., FFJORD, ICLR 2019, arXiv:1810.01367; Chen et al., Neural ODE, arXiv:1806.07366

real_valued_functions: tr(A(s)) along the real interval of integration when A is real-matrix-valued

analytic_domains.statement: A(·) is continuous on a real interval I containing [t0, t] (or vice versa), so a unique C^1 fundamental matrix exists on I
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Hartman, Ordinary Differential Equations; Coddington and Levinson, Theory of Ordinary Differential Equations, Ch. 3; Wikipedia Liouville's formula: 'If the trace of A is a continuous function'

analytic_domains.statement: det(exp(A))=exp(tr(A)) is an identity of entire functions of the entries of A (no spectral restriction)
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 1.13(c); Horn and Johnson, Topics in Matrix Analysis, CUP 1991

analytic_domains.statement: log in log p is the real logarithm on (0, oo); not a complex principal Log of det
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Chen et al., arXiv:1806.07366, instantaneous change of variables written for real densities

branch_conventions: det and tr are polynomials; no branch.
exp(Integral tr A) uses the entire scalar exponential of a well-defined real (or complex) integral.
CNF uses real log of a positive density, not Log det of a complex Jacobian.

limit_domains.statement: Integration of tr(A(s)) is over a compact real interval between t0 and t; A continuous implies the integral exists as a proper Riemann integral
limit_domains.label: DECLARED

source_provenance: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 1.13(c)
Hartman, Ordinary Differential Equations, SIAM Classics, Liouville formula
Jacobi, J. Reine Angew. Math. 22 (1841) 319-359 (derivative of a determinant)

derived_conditions.statement: Specialising Jacobi to Y=Phi with Phi'=A Phi yields (log det Phi)' = tr(A), which integrates to Liouville
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Jacobi formula plus Phi'=A Phi; Wikipedia Liouville's formula proof

derived_conditions.statement: Constant A and Phi(t)=exp(t A), Phi(0)=I, recovers det(exp(t A))=exp(t tr(A))
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED

derived_conditions.statement: Linear CNF f(x)=A x has tr(Df)=tr(A), so d/dt log p = -tr(A) is Liouville for the inverse flow
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Chen et al. instantaneous CoV; Liouville on the Jacobian Phi of the flow

public_source: Liouville's formula: Hartman, Ordinary Differential Equations; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liouville%27s_formula. det(exp(A))=exp(tr(A)): Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Thm 1.13(c). CNF instantaneous CoV: Chen et al., Neural ODE, NeurIPS 2018, arXiv:1806.07366; Grathwohl et al., FFJORD, ICLR 2019, arXiv:1810.01367.
why_not_cse_lgg: CSE can cancel det(diag(e^{alpha t}, e^{beta t})) against e^{(alpha+beta)t} on a 2x2 diagonal probe, but will not identify det o Phi as exp o Integral o tr of the generator, nor unify Jacobi, Liouville, and the CNF log-density ODE as one master. LGG has no det/tr reconstruction.
proposer_leak_risk: Hide: Liouville, Abel, Jacobi formula, Wronskian, CNF, FFJORD, instantaneous change of variables, Neural ODE. Show unlabeled members det(exp(t*A)), exp(t*tr(A)), and the scalar 2x2 residual. Distinct from the Chen adjoint ODE (historical sciml-adjoint-linear-01).
notes: SciML role: continuous normalizing flows; volume Jacobian of a Neural ODE. Catalog: G0001=det(exp(t*A)); G0002=exp(t*tr(A)); G0003=alpha+beta for A=diag(alpha,beta); G0004=exp(alpha*t)*exp(beta*t). NOT sciml-adjoint-linear-01 (Pontryagin adjoint integral for dL/dA). NOT Cauchy-Dunford. Remainder of a CNF trace estimator (Hutchinson) is not this identity.
